new_statements.rule_in_words: In Selau (a Halia dialect) word stress is non-contrastive and by default falls on the penultimate syllable; the author recorded some disyllables with final stress and some trisyllables with initial stress and could not state the conditioning.
new_statements.exceptions: Final stress in some disyllables and initial stress in some trisyllables; conditions 'still unstatable'; no minimal pairs for stress could be found. The same page notes that both vowels and consonants occur long ([wakac] 'think' vs [wa:kac] 'lightning').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, based on elicited citation forms (about six hours of elicitation in Canberra in 1975 with two speakers from Torte village, northern tip of Bougainville). Describes the Selau dialect (Glottolog sela1258 under hali1244), not the central Hanahan dialect described by Allen & Allen.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes SELAU (Glottolog sela1258), which Glottolog 5.1 lists as a dialect of Halia (hali1244) and which Allen & Allen 1987 (as reported by Blust) call a 'sub-language' of Halia spoken on the Selau peninsula, N Bougainville; Blust's data are ~6 hours of elicitation in Canberra in 1975 from two speakers from Torte village. The description of Halia proper (central Hanahan dialect, east Buka) is Allen & Allen 1987 Halia Grammar ch. 2 'Sounds', which could not be fetched sources from our machine (Cloudflare challenge on sil.org file server) and should supersede/confirm this when read.

sources.note: p.147 (sec. 3 'Selau phonology: a first approximation'): stress generally falls on the penult, though final stress in some disyllables and initial stress in some trisyllables was recorded; no minimal pairs found, so stress judged non-phonemic but movable under unstated conditions. Also notes contrastive vowel and consonant length.
